//no-generator: ⚠⚠ THERE IS NO GENERATOR AND THERE MUST NEVER BE ONE. No --update, no --bless, no emit script. The absence is the control. When the verifier refuses, the only two moves are to put the missing thing back or to edit this file by hand, and the second is a review event rather than a keystroke. A regenerate command would make this file certify whatever the tree happens to contain, which is the same defect the fence's .d.ts baseline is written against. The initial rows were laid out once by a throwaway helper in a temp directory that was never committed; from this point the file has no producer.
//what-it-does-not-stop: Nothing here prevents one change editing both the code and this file. The design document says the same of itself. The control is social, resting on a structural absence, and it is the strongest available.
//how-it-is-checked: The verifier compares this against the LIVE inventories the harnesses are about to run — Object.keys(ALL_ARMS) as scripts/run-tests.mjs sees it, and ROWS as scripts/mutate.mjs sees it — never against a second read of the same declaration.
